pages.title: Balancer, load metrics and subtree pinning (MDBalancer, Mantle, export and ephemeral pins)

features.name: Decayed popularity counters (DecayCounter, meta_load)
features.description: Exponentially decayed counters (half-life mds_decay_halflife=5s, values <0.01 snap to 0) in five types IRD/IWR/READDIR/FETCH/STORE; dirfrag scalar meta_load = IRD + 2*IWR + READDIR + 2*FETCH + 4*STORE; four per-dirfrag vectors pop_me, pop_nested, pop_auth_subtree, pop_auth_subtree_nested plus a per-dirfrag LRU of recently hit child dir inodes.
features.notes: CInode::pop (IRD/IWR) is maintained and exported but never read by any decision. mds_decay_halflife is read only at startup.

features.name: Popularity hit accounting on every metadata op
features.description: hit_inode/hit_dir walk from the touched dirfrag to the root updating pop_nested on every level, pop_auth_subtree up to the first subtree root (and pushing inodes onto parents' pop_lru_subdirs), and pop_auth_subtree_nested on all ancestors when the start is auth. Called from getattr/lookup, open, create, setattr/setxattr, readdir (weighted by entries), mknod/mkdir/symlink, link, unlink, rename, cap flush, dirfrag fetch and commit.
features.notes: Every op touches the root dirfrag's counters (global hot spot). Stray dirs are skipped.

features.name: Popularity transfer on migration, subtree changes, rename and split
features.description: subtract_export/add_import move pop_auth_subtree out of/into ancestors' nested counters; CDir encode_export/decode_import ship pop_me and pop_auth_subtree; adjust_subtree_auth/try_subtree_merge_at move pop_auth_subtree across new/merged subtree roots; adjust_pop_for_rename on directory renames; split scales all vectors by 1/2^bits.
features.notes: Split scaling is an acknowledged approximation.

features.name: Per-rank load (mds_load_t) and mds_bal_mode
features.description: get_load sums root dirfrag counters into auth/all vectors and samples req_rate (l_mds_request delta), cpu_load_avg (/proc/self/stat ticks), cache_hit_rate (traverse_hit/traverse) and dispatch queue length; mds_load(mode 0) = 0.8*auth.meta_load + 0.2*all.meta_load + req_rate + 10*queue_len, mode 1 = req_rate + 10*queue_len, mode 2 = cpu_load_avg.
features.notes: Rates refresh only if >=1s since last sample; only computed during heartbeat epochs.

features.name: Heartbeat epoch exchange (MHeartbeat)
features.description: Rank 0 starts an epoch every mds_bal_interval (10s) when balance_automate is set; rank 0 and every active rank that receives rank 0's heartbeat send MHeartbeat(load, beat, import_map) to all other up ranks (non-active ranks drop heartbeats and never answer); each rank plans once it holds one load per in rank. Suppressed while the cluster is degraded or the rank is not active; rank-0 failover restarts epochs at 1.
features.notes: O(N^2) messages per epoch; a stopping rank blocks planning for everyone.

features.name: Default balancer target computation (prep_rebalance)
features.description: Rescales all loads into local meta_load units, target_load = total / |rank mask|, hysteresis via mds_bal_min_rebalance (0.1) and mds_bal_overload_epochs (2), classifies importers (masked, below target) and exporters, matches first against import history, then big-to-big (odd beats) or small-to-big (even beats); only this rank's exports are recorded.
features.notes: Underloaded ranks return before try_rebalance (so they never run idle-import return).

features.name: Export selection (try_rebalance, find_exports)
features.description: Candidates are full-auth subtree roots without own pin/policy/random state; three passes: re-export imports from the target, re-export other imports (5 < pop <= remaining), then recursive dirfrag search over pop_lru_subdirs with need bands (min_start 0.2, need 0.8-1.2, midchunk 0.3, minchunk 0.001) and a 0.1s wall-clock budget; chosen dirfrags go to Migrator::export_dir_nicely.
features.notes: MIN_OFFLOAD=10 and MIN_REEXPORT=5 are hard-coded; targets below 10 or below target_load/(10*|targets|) are skipped.

features.name: Idle import return (mds_bal_idle_threshold)
features.description: When mds_bal_idle_threshold > 0, imported subtrees whose pop_auth_subtree.meta_load is below the threshold are exported back to the parent's rank during try_rebalance.
features.notes: Default 0 (off); only runs on overloaded ranks inside an epoch.

features.name: balance_automate file system flag
features.description: MDSMap flag CEPH_MDSMAP_BALANCE_AUTOMATE (bit 8), set by 'ceph fs set <fs> balance_automate <bool>', default off for new and existing file systems; it only gates rank 0 starting heartbeat epochs.
features.notes: Mantle and idle-import return are also gated because they run inside epochs.

features.name: bal_rank_mask
features.description: MDSMap string (default '-1'): hex bitmask of ranks the balancer may move load to; '0'/'0x0' disables planning; '-1'/'all'/invalid means all ranks with count=max_mds; unmasked ranks are exporters with target 0 and shed all unpinned load.
features.notes: Popcount includes nonexistent ranks; >16 hex digits mis-parsed unless multiple of 16.

features.name: Mantle Lua balancer
features.description: MDSMap 'balancer' names a RADOS object in the metadata pool holding a Lua script; read synchronously (timeout mds_bal_interval/2) on name change, executed per epoch in a fresh lua_State with globals whoami and mds[0..n-1] metrics; must return a table with exactly n integer-keyed numeric entries (load to send per rank); failures fall back to prep_rebalance with a cluster-log warning.
features.notes: Documented as experimental/not for production; blocks the dispatch thread under mds_lock.

features.name: Export target publication (MMDSLoadTargets / export_targets)
features.description: Per-rank DecayCounters (half-life mds_bal_target_decay=10) hit by the Migrator at each export step and by bystander notify acks; every tick (active/stopping) update_targets drops expired ranks and sends MMDSLoadTargets(gid, set<int32>) to the mon when the MDSMap export_targets set differs; exports wait until dest appears in the map (cancel after 4 maps).
features.notes: Clients pre-open sessions to export targets; kclient reconnects to export targets in up:reconnect even without a session.

features.name: Export pin vxattr ceph.dir.pin (set/remove)
features.description: SETXATTR on a directory (not root) with an int32 rank; <0 means unpin (-1), >=256 EDOM, unparsable EINVAL, non-dir/root EINVAL, missing 'p' MDS cap EACCES; RMXATTR unpins (no-op if unset); journaled via EUpdate with policylock xlock; bumps ctime/change_attr/rctime.
features.notes: SETXATTR with no value (CEPH_XATTR_REMOVE) is EINVAL; only RMXATTR removes.

features.name: Pin read-back (InodeStat dir_pin, GETVXATTR)
features.description: InodeStat v2+ carries dir_pin = the inode's own export_pin (-1 unset), which kclient/libcephfs expose as ceph.dir.pin; ceph.dir.pin.random and .distributed are read with CEPH_MDS_OP_GETVXATTR returning default-formatted double and 0/1 strings; non-directories get ENODATA.
features.notes: Inherited and ephemeral placement is never reported to clients. GETVXATTR needs session feature CEPHFS_FEATURE_OP_GETVXATTR (17).

features.name: Pin inheritance and precedence resolution
features.description: CInode::get_export_pin walks toward the root (stopping at system inodes such as the root, inodes without a parent dentry, and inodes with nlink 0): closest explicit pin wins, then a distributed policy (hash of the policy dir ino and the dirfrag holding the path), then random-pinned state honored only if the first policy above it is random; inherit=false reports only the inode's own setting.
features.notes: Documented to users in doc/cephfs/multimds.rst (closest parent rule).

features.name: Pin enforcement (handle_export_pins, aux subtrees, delayed pins)
features.description: Each tick: pass 1 processes export_pin_queue per auth dirfrag (split dist frags below minimum, mark/create AUXSUBTREE subtree roots for local targets, export non-empty dirfrags to remote targets, clear AUX when unpinned, park pins >= max_mds in the delayed queue); pass 2 exports every auth subtree whose inherited pin is another valid rank. AUXSUBTREE roots are never merged into parent subtrees.
features.notes: Empty dirfrags are never moved by pins; pins are asynchronous (next tick).

features.name: Distributed ephemeral pins (ceph.dir.pin.distributed)
features.description: Boolean policy (inode flags bit 0, strict_strtob grammar) that forces the directory to at least ceil(log2(factor*max_mds)) frag bits (factor mds_export_ephemeral_distributed_factor=2; 0 bits when max_mds <= 1) and places each dirfrag f on hash_into_rank_bucket(ino, f); children and their subtrees follow the dirfrag holding their dentry; merges below the minimum are blocked.
features.notes: Used by mgr volumes 'fs subvolumegroup pin <vol> <grp> distributed 1' to spread subvolumes; spread is per name-hash bucket, not per subvolume.

features.name: Random ephemeral pins (ceph.dir.pin.random)
features.description: Double policy in [0,1] capped by mds_export_ephemeral_random_max (0.01); directories created by mkdir or loaded by a dirfrag fetch below the policy are pinned with that probability to hash_into_rank_bucket(ino); state kept in memory, journaled as EMetaBlob fullbit STATE_EPHEMERAL_RANDOM, exported and replicated; re-rolled after cache drop.
features.notes: Setting the policy re-evaluates nothing; NaN passes validation; value > max returns EINVAL, outside [0,1] EDOM.

features.name: Consistent hash into rank bucket
features.description: rjhash64(ino) (plus rjhash64 of the frag value for non-root frags) fed into Lamping-Veach jump consistent hash over max_mds buckets.
features.notes: Bucket count is max_mds, not active ranks; frags with equal value at different depths hash identically.

features.name: Ephemeral pin redistribution on max_mds / config change
features.description: On every MDSMap the delayed pin queue is rescanned; when max_mds changes all ephemerally pinned inodes are re-evaluated and the distributed minimum frag bits recomputed; toggling mds_export_ephemeral_distributed/random re-evaluates all ephemeral pins.
features.notes: Re-evaluation happens before the new minimum frag bits are computed.

features.name: Stopping-rank subtree handoff interplay with pins
features.description: A stopping rank (never rank 0) runs handle_export_pins itself and exports every non-ephemerally-pinned auth subtree to its parent inode's authority, replacing any destination > 0 that is not up:active (including the stopping rank itself) with rank 0; export_dir ignores pins while stopping.
features.notes: Nested same-rank subtrees (e.g. /a and /a/b both pinned to the stopping rank) go to rank 0 because the stopping rank is not active, so the dest != whoami assert in export_dir is not reached on this path.

features.name: Fragmentation triggers from the balancer
features.description: maybe_fragment queues delayed (mds_bal_fragment_interval=5s) splits when size > mds_bal_split_size (10000) or the dirfrag is read/write hot (25000/10000), fast splits when already pending and > 1.5x split size, and delayed merges below mds_bal_merge_size (50); callbacks call MDCache::split_dir/merge_dir.
features.notes: Root, mdsdir and stray dirs are excluded here; stray dirs are fragmented via advance_stray.

features.name: Directory size limit (ENOSPC at mds_bal_fragment_size_max)
features.description: Creates (openc, mknod, mkdir, symlink), links and renames into a dirfrag whose projected fragstat size is >= mds_bal_fragment_size_max (100000, cached in Server) fail with ENOSPC; unlink/rmdir/rename that need a new stray dentry fail the same way when the chosen stray dirfrag is at the limit (not for replayed requests).
features.notes: Client-visible error; the root directory never fragments so it is limited to one dirfrag.

features.name: Hot-directory replication (REP_ALL, MDirUpdate)
features.description: Read-hot auth dirfrags (pop_auth_subtree + 10*pop_me >= mds_bal_replicate_threshold 8000) are marked REP_ALL and announced with MDirUpdate to every active non-replica rank, which discovers the path and becomes a replica; reply traces list replicas in DirStat dist so clients spread USE_ANY_MDS reads.
features.notes: Unreplication threshold defaults to 0 (never); dir_rep is not persisted to RADOS (it travels in exports, replica encodings and rejoin) and the root starts REP_ALL only at mkfs. DirStat dist is sent only while mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth (default false) is off; kclient uses dist only for requests routed by dentry name hash.

features.name: dump loads admin command
features.description: asok/tell 'dump loads [depth]' prints per-dirfrag popularity vectors (BFS from root) and the last epoch's mds_load, mds_meta_load and mds_import_map.

features.name: get subtrees admin command
features.description: asok/tell 'get subtrees' lists subtree roots with is_auth, auth_first, auth_second, export_pin, distributed_ephemeral_pin, random_ephemeral_pin, export_pin_target and the dir dump.
features.notes: Used heavily by qa test_exports to assert pin placement.

features.name: export dir admin command
features.description: asok/tell 'export dir <path> <rank>' starts Migrator::export_dir for frag 0 of a cached auth directory; returns -ENOENT/-EINVAL for bad target/path, else 0 even if the export is refused.
features.notes: Pins still veto silently.

features.name: Balancer perf counters
features.description: mds.load_cent, mds.q (set per heartbeat), mds.subtrees (per tick), mds.exported/imported and exported_inodes/imported_inodes (Migrator), mds.dir_split/dir_merge, mds_cache.dir_update/dir_update_receipt/dir_try_discover.
features.notes: Dashboard and telemetry read subtrees and *_inodes; exported/imported/q are DEBUGONLY priority (not sent to mgr by default); qa check-counter uses exported/imported and dir_update counters.

features.name: mgr volumes subvolume/subvolumegroup pin
features.description: 'ceph fs subvolumegroup pin <vol> <group> <export|distributed|random> <setting>' and 'ceph fs subvolume pin <vol> <sub> <type> <setting> [<group>]' convert the setting (int, strtobool->0/1, float) and setxattr ceph.dir.pin* on /volumes/<group> or /volumes/<group|_nogroup>/<subvol> via libcephfs, passing MDS errors back.
features.notes: The _nogroup group cannot be pinned (EPERM); pins are never read back by the mgr.

features.name: Balancer/pin configuration options
features.description: mds_bal_* (interval, mode, thresholds, split/merge sizes, fragment interval/fast factor/size max, export_pin, target_decay, idle_threshold, max/max_until), mds_export_ephemeral_* (distributed, distributed_factor, random, random_max), mds_decay_halflife, mds_max_export_size; tracked keys are applied under mds_lock via the finisher.
features.notes: Most are dev-level; defaults listed on the page.

features.name: Mantle cluster log messages
features.description: Cluster log WRN 'using old balancer; mantle failed for balancer=<name> : <strerror>' on every failing epoch and INF 'mantle balancer version changed: <name>' from rank 0 on successful load.
features.notes: qa test_mantle.py greps these strings (suite not scheduled).

features.name: Testing hooks (mds_thrash_exports, mds_thrash_fragments)
features.description: Dev options that make the dispatch loop export random dirfrags to random active ranks and split/merge random dirfrags; mds_thrash_exports also disables the planned rebalance.

serialization_points.name: Popularity hit walk to the root
serialization_points.shared_state: DecayCounters of every ancestor dirfrag (root included) and parents' pop_lru_subdirs
serialization_points.why_serialized: plain fields mutated under mds_lock on every op
serialization_points.notes: Additive and commutative; staleness tolerated by all consumers.

serialization_points.name: All balancer planning and selection under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: subtree map, dirfrag popularity, LRUs, Migrator queue
serialization_points.why_serialized: runs on the dispatch thread inside handle_heartbeat
serialization_points.notes: Plans are approximate; could run on a snapshot.

serialization_points.name: find_exports cache walk with 0.1s budget
serialization_points.why_serialized: recursive walk of live cache under mds_lock; budget exists because it stalls the rank

serialization_points.name: Mantle synchronous RADOS read
serialization_points.why_serialized: dispatch thread waits up to mds_bal_interval/2 for the Objecter while holding mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: Repeated every epoch while the read fails.

serialization_points.name: Mantle Lua execution
serialization_points.why_serialized: runs inline in handle_heartbeat under mds_lock with no time or memory limit

serialization_points.name: Heartbeat epoch barrier
serialization_points.why_serialized: planning requires one load per in rank for the same epoch driven by rank 0
serialization_points.notes: Any stopping/silent rank blocks rebalancing cluster-wide.

serialization_points.name: Pin enforcement scan per tick
serialization_points.why_serialized: single tick under mds_lock scans the queue and every auth subtree (walking to the root for each)

serialization_points.name: Delayed pin queue rescan on every MDSMap
serialization_points.why_serialized: map handling under mds_lock iterates all delayed and (on max_mds change) all ephemeral pins

serialization_points.name: Pin policy write
serialization_points.why_serialized: xlock policylock + rdlock snaplocks, journal EUpdate
serialization_points.notes: Conflicts only with other policy/layout/quota changes on the same inode.

serialization_points.name: Export-target publication round trip
serialization_points.why_serialized: an export waits until the mon has committed dest into this rank's export_targets
serialization_points.notes: Clients rely on export_targets for pre-connect and reconnect; Paxos commit per change.

serialization_points.name: Migrator export queue throttle and per-round clear
serialization_points.why_serialized: rank-wide size budget (2 x mds_max_export_size) and queue reset at each planning round

serialization_points.name: Split/merge debounce and dirfrag freeze
serialization_points.why_serialized: delayed by mds_bal_fragment_interval then freezes the dirfrag for the fragment op
serialization_points.notes: Fast splits run on the progress thread after the current dispatch.

serialization_points.name: Hot-dir replication broadcast
serialization_points.why_serialized: decided inline in hit_dir under mds_lock; receivers discover under their mds_lock

serialization_points.name: Config change fan-out
serialization_points.shared_state: cached bal_* and ephemeral options, ephemeral pin re-evaluation
serialization_points.why_serialized: finisher lambda takes mds_lock and re-evaluates all ephemeral pins on toggle

external_contract.detail: Sent synchronously to the auth MDS with raw value bytes. Grammar: pin int32 (<0 unpin, >=256 EDOM, else EINVAL on parse error); random double in [0,1] (EDOM) and <= mds_export_ephemeral_random_max (EINVAL); distributed true/false or integer. Directory only and not root (EINVAL); 'p' MDS cap required (EACCES); ESTALE if the inode is not cached. Success bumps ctime/change_attr (rctime raised); the client usually returns on the early unsafe reply sent before the EUpdate commits.
removexattr(2) arrives as RMXATTR and resets to -1 / 0 / false; returns 0 without journaling if already unset. SETXATTR with CEPH_XATTR_REMOVE (NULL value) fails with EINVAL.

InodeStat struct v2+ field dir_pin = own export_pin (int32, -1 unset); client caches it as i_dir_pin (auth or newer replies only) and returns it for getxattr ceph.dir.pin after a forced GETATTR; hidden from listxattr.

CEPH_MDS_OP_GETVXATTR (0x00106) to the auth MDS; requires CEPHFS_FEATURE_OP_GETVXATTR (17) in the session feature bits else the client returns ENODATA; reply_extra_bl = versioned(1,1) string: default ostream double for random, '0'/'1' for distributed, integer for pin; ENODATA on non-directories.
Per-rank export_targets in mds_info_t: client opens sessions to targets of laggy ranks and sends reconnects to targets entering up:reconnect even without a prior session.

external_contract.item: DirStat auth/dist after migration and replication
external_contract.detail: Reply traces and readdir replies carry frag, auth and dist (replicas plus auth, only from the auth rank and only while mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth is off) per dirfrag; kclient keeps up to 4 dist entries and sends USE_ANY_MDS requests routed by dentry name hash to a random active, non-laggy dist rank, otherwise to the auth.

Create/mknod/mkdir/symlink/link/rename into a dirfrag with >= mds_bal_fragment_size_max (100000) entries returns ENOSPC; unlink/rmdir/rename needing a stray dentry in a full stray dirfrag returns ENOSPC too.
Same SETXATTR/RMXATTR/GETVXATTR semantics; ceph.dir.pin from cached Inode::dir_pin (auth or newer replies); other pin names via _getvxattr.

connect_mds_targets opens sessions to a rank's export_targets that are clientreplay/active/stopping: on session open, on each map in which that rank's state changes to active or later, and before reconnect.

MSG_MDS_OFFLOAD_TARGETS 0x20a: PaxosServiceMessage header (version 0), u64 global_id, set<int32> targets; requires mon cap 'mds x'; mon stores it in mds_info_t::export_targets for a gid holding a rank, ignores unchanged sets, never replies.

Mon-owned fields the MDS must accept and interpret: flags bit 8 balance_automate, string balancer (Mantle object name, ev>=11), string bal_rank_mask (default '-1', ev>=17, validated by hex2bin), max_mds; printed by fs dump/get.

fs subvolumegroup pin / fs subvolume pin call setxattr through the mgr's libcephfs mount on /volumes/<group> or /volumes/<group|_nogroup>/<subvol> with str(int), '0'/'1', or str(float); MDS errnos are returned to the CLI.

Dashboard requests mds.exported, mds.exported_inodes, mds.imported, mds.imported_inodes, mds.subtrees; telemetry sums mds.subtrees; exported/imported are DEBUGONLY and not sent with default mgr_stats_threshold 5.
Whole-object read of the object named by MDSMap 'balancer' from the metadata pool, default namespace; nothing else written by the balancer.

external_contract.item: get subtrees / dump loads / export dir asok
external_contract.detail: qa test_exports parses get subtrees fields (is_auth, auth_first, auth_second, export_pin, distributed_ephemeral_pin, random_ephemeral_pin, export_pin_target, dir.path); dump loads JSON layout; export dir returns {return_code}.
Multi-rank workload suites require mds.exported/mds.imported > 0 and mds_cache.dir_update/dir_update_receipt >= 3 when mds_bal_replicate_threshold=1.
WRN 'using old balancer; mantle failed for balancer=<name> : <strerror>' and INF 'mantle balancer version changed: <name>'.

rust_implications.implication: MHeartbeat, MDirUpdate, load formulas, the epoch protocol, hysteresis, selection heuristics, the jump hash and AUXSUBTREE are internal to C++ MDS clusters; since the Rust MDS never coexists with C++ daemons it may replace all of them. The hard contracts are the three ceph.dir.pin* vxattrs (grammar, errnos, side effects), InodeStat dir_pin, GETVXATTR formatting, DirStat auth/dist, ENOSPC at the dirfrag limit, MMDSLoadTargets/export_targets, the MDSMap fields balance_automate/balancer/bal_rank_mask/max_mds, the mgr-consumed perf counters and the asok outputs used by qa.

ceph.dir.pin maps naturally onto 'place shard S on rank r'; the Rust Shard Manager can treat each pinned directory as a stable shard boundary (the C++ aux subtree) and must keep the closest-ancestor precedence (explicit > distributed > random) because users and docs rely on it.

mgr/volumes 'distributed 1' on a subvolume group spreads subvolumes by a hash of their names over the group directory's dirfrags (at least 2^ceil(log2(2*max_mds)) of them, each placed by a jump hash over max_mds), not one rank per subvolume. A Rust MDS with per-subvolume shards can spread per subvolume instead (externally only placement is visible), but must still accept and persist the flag and report it via GETVXATTR.

Every C++ op updates counters on every ancestor up to the root under mds_lock. Per-shard (per-subvolume) counters aggregated periodically give the same information without a global write path; no peer observes these counters except through dump loads/load_cent.
The C++ balancer stalls whenever any in rank is stopping or silent. Load reports can be gossiped asynchronously with timestamps; planning only needs an approximate snapshot.

A first Rust MDS can implement static placement only (explicit + ephemeral pins) and treat balance_automate/Mantle as unsupported or no-op while staying compatible: the flag only gates rank-0-driven dynamic balancing in C++.

Mantle is experimental, gated by balance_automate and blocks the dispatch thread on RADOS and Lua. If supported at all it should load asynchronously and run sandboxed with limits; the only external surface is the MDSMap 'balancer' string, the metadata-pool object and two cluster-log strings.

Clients pre-open sessions to export_targets and the kclient reconnects to targets in up:reconnect even without a session; any cross-rank shard move that migrates client caps should first publish the destination via MMDSLoadTargets (and keep it for ~100 s) to preserve kclient recovery behavior.

C++ re-resolves the inherited pin of every auth subtree by walking to the root on every tick. A Rust design can store the effective placement per shard and recompute only on policy change, max_mds change or shard split.

C++ hashes into max_mds buckets (not active ranks), so pins may target ranks that cannot accept exports and are retried each tick; the Rust MDS is free to choose its own mapping but should keep minimal movement on max_mds changes because users expect it (docs).

rust_implications.topic: Random ephemeral pins are probabilistic and non-durable
rust_implications.implication: C++ rolls at mkdir/fetch time and re-rolls after cache drop (journal-only persistence). A Rust implementation may persist the decision or derive it deterministically from the inode number; only the policy value is externally visible.

Distributed pins force fragmentation of tiny directories only to obtain hash buckets; a Rust MDS that shards by name hash need not fragment for placement, but dirfrag identifiers/auth still appear in client replies (see dirfrags page) and ENOSPC at 100000 entries per dirfrag is client-visible.

Replica serving of reads (DirStat dist list) is optional for correctness; if implemented, replicas must remain consistent under the lock protocol. The qa replication suite checks mds_cache.dir_update counters, which a Rust MDS would either emulate or not be tested by.

rust_implications.topic: Per-subvolume autonomy and the stopping path
rust_implications.implication: C++ stopping ranks push subtrees back to parents and ignore pins; a Rust shard model should hand off whole shards atomically (2PC) and must handle pins that target a stopping rank (C++ parks pins >= max_mds in a delayed queue).

mgr volumes surfaces MDS errnos verbatim (EINVAL, EDOM, EACCES); Rust must return the same codes for the same inputs, including EINVAL for SETXATTR with CEPH_XATTR_REMOVE on pin vxattrs and EINVAL for random values above mds_export_ephemeral_random_max.

Keep perf counters mds.subtrees, mds.exported(_inodes), mds.imported(_inodes) with the same names because dashboard/telemetry read them; 'get subtrees' JSON is consumed by qa test_exports if those tests are reused.

The C++ MDS already sends an empty dist list when mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth is set, and clients then route everything to the auth rank. A Rust MDS without read replicas can always send an empty dist (and auth = owning rank) without breaking kclient or libcephfs routing.

open_questions: Resolved during review: MDCache::shutdown_pass does not hit the Migrator::export_dir dest != whoami assert for nested same-rank subtrees, because it replaces any non-active destination (including the stopping rank itself) with rank 0. Remaining open: a Mantle script returning >= 10 for its own rank reaches export_dir(dir, self) and that assert (code reading only; test_mantle.py is not scheduled by any suite).
After failover, are same-auth subtree roots recreated from ESubtreeMap merged before handle_export_pins re-marks them AUXSUBTREE? Not traced in this step.
Rook's subvolume-group pinning is assumed to call 'ceph fs subvolumegroup pin'; not verifiable from this repository.
NFS-Ganesha has no pin-specific usage as far as known; not verified against Ganesha sources.
Should the Rust MDS reproduce 'get subtrees'/'dump loads' JSON exactly, or only what qa tests parse?
localize_balancer waits on a condition variable without a predicate and C_SafeCond references stack variables; correctness after op_cancel relies on Objecter cancellation semantics (not traced).

When a dirfrag is already an aux subtree on its hashed rank, a max_mds change that raises the distributed minimum frag bits may not requeue the inode (queue_export_pin runs with the old minimum), leaving it under-split until something else requeues it. Code reading only.
